_readme: User-visible changes in the replacement app, newest first.

entries.summary: Passwordless accounts on staging with Google and email codes
detail: Staging uses Clerk sign-in without password creation or guest mode.
Signed-in accounts save progress in a separate staging database, with server checks for account ownership.
Existing production accounts and progress are unchanged. Staging accounts start with empty progress.
Sign-up stays inside Fluency, with readable sign-in controls and a scrollable layout on small screens.

entries.summary: Desktop sidebar for choosing sets, with a focused study view
detail: Desktop setup has a left sidebar for choosing sets, Your words, progress, tutorial, settings and account.
Settings, learning context and progress fill the workspace beside the sidebar; setup sheets no longer dock in the gutters.
Starting a set hides navigation and restores the existing study side panels. Returning to the main menu restores the sidebar.
Phones and narrow windows retain the compact top bar and dialogs.
Checked desktop setup, workspace navigation, study entry/exit and phone layout; app tests pass.

entries.summary: Clearer flashcards, lyrics and progress, with a preferred AI setting
detail: Tap companion lemma/POS pills on the front to switch readings; known meanings stay greyed and the front explains what remains to practise.
Brighter, lighter POS pills; aligned from labels; commonness appears before sense subrows and information follows them.
Larger artist photos and flags on progress screens; artist sources keep their own imagery.
Choose ChatGPT or Claude in Account settings and open its sign-in page; the preference chooses the lyric-view logo.
Larger English lyrics, level labels in study navigation and options, and word totals in the level scrubber.
Reuse the deployed Fλ icon throughout the app and give the startup language chooser a full-width placement.
Tutorial and unrelated in-progress edits are excluded from this staging commit.

entries.summary: The tutorial fills a phone screen: the card spans the full width and the explanation never moves the card
detail: Phone tutorial is full-bleed: no modal inset or rounded corners; title and exit share one row.
The tallest explanation's height is reserved once (measured at the coach's real width, including a chapter's two-button last note), so changing steps cannot move the card or the navigation.
A card that has to shrink is laid out at stage width ÷ scale, so it still spans the stage instead of sitting in a narrow strip; height cap raised to 760 px.
Work left uncommitted by the tutorial (SHOWCASE) chat; committed and staged on Josh's instruction after a phone-width smoke check.

entries.summary: Song translation: a play bar, tap-a-line to play, an English toggle, 389 more songs, and a tidier entity box
detail: Play bar at the bottom: previous line, play/pause, next line, and repeat this line. Repeat loops the line being sung, or the next one you tap. On a phone using Spotify's app, the highlight is kept in step by polling Spotify about every 1.5 s.
Tap anywhere on a line to play it from there (tapping a word still opens its card; the Spotify button still works).
EN button in the header hides or shows the English under each line; it is remembered on this device.

The song list grows from 30 to 419 songs: all of Bad Bunny, Rosalía and Young Miko in the lyrics release that LRCLIB has timed lyrics for (389 of 401). Search covers all of them; a song's lyrics are fetched when it is opened. 10 of them rest on a single LRCLIB record, so their timing is the least certain.
Song links now carry the song's Spotify id instead of its position in the list, so a saved link no longer shifts after importing a song. Old numeric links still open the song they used to.
Entity boxes are now a tight rectangle (4 px corners) that wraps the name, and the Wiktionary mark is a serif W at the start of the entity instead of the end.
Yonaguni's human translations load on the deployed site now: the build excluded the folder they were read from, so they never appeared there. They now match 51 of 60 lines.
Removed unused wiring: previous/next-song buttons, the compatibility anchors and the count badges.

entries.summary: Smart Skip is one line on every screen, and the level picker takes the language's (or artist's) colour
detail: Smart Skip on: the count moves up beside the name and the examples follow it, e.g. 'Smart Skip  3,115 skipped  e.g. idea, familia, minutos, importante, capitán'. The second 'N words skipped' line is gone.
At most five examples, set in the same type and colour as the level box's 'e.g.' line, and no trailing '...'. A narrow row shows fewer words, or none, rather than a cut-off list.

Phones get the same single line: name and Recommended badge when off, name and count when on (the 'Fewer cards, same coverage' line no longer has room and is dropped). Row height is 66px in every state; checked at 320, 375 and 800 wide in Speech and in Lyrics.
The selected level badge and its glow were fixed blue; they now use the language colour (Spanish red) or the artist's colour (Bad Bunny blue).

entries.summary: Song translation: catalogue songs now play from any line, the line being sung fills green, and the song list is just song and artist
detail: All 30 catalogue songs carry their Spotify track and LRCLIB line timing, baked offline (scripts/bake_probe_timings.py): 30 of 30 have a track, 29 of 30 have timing. Soso - Remix has no matching timed lyrics, so it stays plain with no play buttons.

While Spotify plays, the current line is highlighted and its words turn green as they are reached; finished lines dim. Word timing is estimated from each word's length within its line, because LRCLIB times lines, not words.

The view scrolls to the line being sung and stops following for four seconds when you scroll yourself. If Spotify is playing a different cut of the song (length differs by over 3 s) the highlight turns off and says so.
Songs with no Spotify track or no timing show no play buttons and no explanatory banner.
Song list shows only song and artist: the number, the line count, the ONLINE badge and the 'Curated Catalog' header are gone.
Yonaguni's human translations are matched to the timed lines by text (28 exact, more by near-match), so they no longer drift when the lines change.

entries.summary: Czech level coverage is now right for every level, and opening a deck does less repeated work
detail: Level coverage read each card's share under its dictionary form (ten) instead of the word actually spoken (to). Czech level 1 showed 32.0% of speech; it is 43.9%. Level 31 showed 0.9%; it is 0.3%.
Czech coverage now covers all 10,000 deck words (rebuilt from the same OpenSubtitles 2018 counts for release v22), so levels 31 to 100 show a figure.
Smart Skip works out its categories once per burst of work instead of about a dozen times when a deck opens: setup work on opening Czech ~800 ms to ~460 ms.
The hidden loading spinner no longer animates behind the app.

entries.summary: Sessions are now chosen by time, and Go explains what to do when a level has little or nothing new left
detail: Go and Practise share one session length: 5 min, 10 min or No limit. Tap the clock chip to change it; it is remembered on this device.
Time becomes cards at a fixed assumed pace (about 15 s per new card, 10 s per practice card): 5 min = 20 new or 30 practice cards.
When more of a level waits in Practise than is new (at least 10), Go asks: practise these, or learn the new ones. It asks once per level until the app reloads.
When a level has no new words left, Go shows either 'No new words left' (practise, next level, or redo) or 'You've mastered all the words' (next level, or redo).
Practice Errors is now Practise. It says how many words are waiting and when the next ones come back, e.g. 'Nothing to practise. 12 words come back tomorrow, 30 more this week.'
The level badge shows the word range only; the level total appears while you scrub the bar, and the deck size is in the Choose a Level help.
End of session: 'Keep going · 5 min' replaces 'Another 20'; finishing a level says how many words are waiting in Practise.

entries.summary: Go starts a session almost at once: its words and example sentences download while you're on the home screen
detail: The home screen now starts the session's downloads (word rows and example sentences, ~1.5 MB for a Czech level) as soon as it shows Go.
Before, Go waited for them: about 2.5 s on production for Czech level 1. Timed locally after the change: 0.2 s, with nothing left to download.
Uses the same prefetch the end-of-session screen already used for the next session; repeat renders do not download twice.

entries.summary: Opening a deck freezes the screen for less time: Smart Skip stops re-reading your language settings for every word
detail: Smart Skip asked which languages you read once per word (~140,000 times when a deck opened), re-reading and re-parsing two saved settings each time.
The answer is now worked out once per pass and dropped the moment either setting changes.
Czech, timed locally: Smart Skip refresh 817 ms to 214 ms; Smart Skip button 239 ms to 101 ms; skipped-word list 74 ms to 24 ms.

entries.summary: Czech coverage figures now show on Staging, and Staging no longer floods the browser with requests
detail: Staging answers missing files with a real 404. Before, Cloudflare returned the app page with relative preload links, which recursed without end (~500 requests a minute per open tab).
Commit the Czech coverage file (coverage/cs/coverage.json) to the app, byte-identical to the one production already serves, so Staging builds it too.

entries.summary: Smart Skip is easier to browse; lyric credits put the song above the artist
detail: Keep the cognate explanation open initially; other explanations stay folded. Mobile groups secondary controls under Other settings.
Group category, search and known-language filters; show live match counts and the exact number of words the supplementary study button will load.
Use a direct language picker instead of cycling. Empty comparisons remain selectable so learners can switch back.
Keep desktop settings and browser controls accessible while scrolling; add preview chevrons to word rows.
Render song titles without italics, above artist or vocalist credits, in both live cards and tutorial replicas.
All 268 app tests passed; desktop scrolling, phone layout, five-match study counts and two-line card credits checked in the browser.

entries.summary: Artist photos in progress; flags and language codes in Smart Skip
detail: Music progress uses the active artist picture, with initials or a music symbol when artwork is unavailable. Speech keeps its language flag.
Smart Skip column headings show flags beside ES, EN and other language codes. Multiple known languages show their own labels rather than a globe.
The cognate language filter uses All or a specific flag and code; unknown languages keep their code without a globe icon.
All 268 app tests passed; artist header and cognate columns checked in the browser.

entries.summary: Simpler language picker and consistent modal close buttons
detail: Centre Save text and replace duplicate modal Cancel actions with the standard header X.
Remove Add another language; use only listed profile choices.
Label listed languages without study decks Coming soon while keeping them selectable as languages you know.
Preserve existing saved language profiles and Smart Skip’s relevant-pair filtering.

entries.summary: Lyrics vocabulary now shares Smart Skip with Speech; Artist Extras and the 60% gate are folded away
detail: Browse supplementary song vocabulary by category inside Smart Skip, with shared search, lyric previews and sessions of up to 20 cards.
Remove the separate Extras panel and unlock requirement; older Extra links now open Smart Skip.
Use consistent optional skip defaults and restore saved supplementary cards by their original identities.
Explain Song Lines on tap, correct supplementary rank totals, update Music/Speech naming and shared study help.
Preserve the selected language when switching from Music to Speech.
Verified phone layout and supplementary card navigation; all 268 app tests pass.

entries.summary: New home-screen icon: white Fλ on an indigo-to-violet square; the app is called Fluency again (staging: Fβ, Fluency β)
detail: Icon is a white F with a smaller λ beside it on a deep indigo to violet gradient (Manrope). Placeholder until a real logo is chosen.
Production is named Fluency; staging is Fluency β with Fβ, so the two installs are told apart.
The iPhone home-screen icon is the 512-pixel render, so it stays sharp when iOS scales it.
Phones that already added the app keep the old icon and name until it is removed and re-added.

entries.summary: Smart Skip offers useful language pairs, with missing maps marked Coming soon
detail: An explicit pair list now limits both runtime filtering and offline mapping generation.
Smart Skip shows only relevant languages; relevant unmapped pairs are greyed out as Coming soon.
The filtered Languages you know editor preserves unrelated profile languages and links to the full list in Settings.
Onboarding and general Settings can save other languages by name or code without creating unnecessary mappings.

entries.summary: Keep language-profile and BRIDGE preferences isolated during staging review
detail: Language-profile and Smart Skip preference writes now use the staging account namespace.
Added regression checks for both preference writers so staging review cannot update production preferences.

entries.summary: BRIDGE and shared known-language settings, with safer verb matching and centred mobile dialogs
detail: Languages you know now live in Settings → App, save across the account and are asked once; Polish is always offered.
Smart Skip source-language choices no longer overwrite the shared profile.
BRIDGE is opt-in per learning language and uses known matching source meanings without writing target progress; skipped words remain browsable.
Cross-language verbs require compatible dictionary forms, including person, number, tense, mood and lexical aspect. Infinitives do not imply knowing conjugated forms.
Spanish/French/Portuguese mappings are tied to exact releases. French currently has 200 cards, so verified BRIDGE eligibility is limited.
Mobile dialogs are vertically centred; desktop panels fit the side gutter or centre when there is insufficient space.
Smart Skip title, Recommended badge, info icon and larger toggle share a line, with smaller explanation below.

entries.summary: Home-screen icon is now just the glowing F and β (no inner tile), and Add to Home Screen should stop offering the old Flashcards name
detail: Icon drops the inner rounded square: a larger periwinkle F with a small β (α on staging), glowing on the dark background.
The manifest link now carries a version tag, so a phone still running the previous app version fetches the new manifest instead of its cached "Flashcards" one.

entries.summary: Progress uses stronger colours and shows the cards left to study first.
detail: Changed the washed-out palette to the Portuguese level accent green, vivid yellow, white, violet and slate; made legend text more readable.
The continuous bar and its legend now run New, Practice, Known, Estimated familiar, Skipped, putting the work remaining on the left.
Session selection, level boundaries, estimation and saved learning progress are unchanged.

entries.summary: Level progress is now one continuous bar with lighter status colours.
detail: Removed the four progress divisions and grouped each learning status into one continuous stretch instead of repeating colours across rank regions.
Known cards are light green, practice is light yellow, new is white, estimated familiarity is soft lilac and skipped is blue-grey. Legend colours match in both themes.
Kept 100-card target levels, 20-card sessions, saved progress and within-level estimation unchanged.

entries.summary: Rare uses has a monochrome count in a thin circle instead of a coloured notification badge.
detail: Removed the coloured fill and shadow behind the Rare uses count.
Count remains above the icon at the top left, with white digits and a thin white ring; light mode uses dark ink.
Kept the three-bar icon and its half-filled first bar.

entries.summary: Card actions sit directly on the page background, with less padding and more room for card content.
detail: Removed the action row’s coloured background and rounded tray in both themes; it now blends into the page like the scrubber.
Reduced the gap and button padding, preserving readable labels and usable tap targets.
Reclaimed footer space: about 30px more card content on desktop and 42px on phones, while respecting the phone safe area.

entries.summary: Commonness tooltips stay above the card without clipping; white text and taller sense meters.
detail: Commonness explanations open in a separate overlay above scrolling and transformed card surfaces, positioned within the screen edges.
Tooltip text and commonness icon are white. Sense-row meters are taller and slightly wider, with less surrounding padding.
Hover, tap and keyboard access work; tooltips dismiss when scrolling, flipping, changing cards or returning to the menu.

entries.summary: SETWISE: one level progress bar and short 20-card sessions, with finer starting-level suggestions.
detail: Keep 100-card target levels; four quiet progress segments replace the selectable 25-card boxes. Go starts up to 20 eligible cards across the level.
Session completion offers Another 20 (or the smaller remaining count) and waits for your choice. New cards and practice remain separate.
Estimation suggests positions such as around halfway through Level 1 while preserving the saved starting rank. Estimated familiarity is shown separately from answered-card progress.
Resume retains saved session membership and order, including old sessions and companion cards. Guest sessions advance in memory without syncing answers.

entries.summary: Clearer Rare uses badge and Flag a meaning counter, with a softer card action tray.
detail: Rare uses count moves to the top left with larger digits, and its first bar is half filled in white.
Mark a meaning becomes Flag a meaning. Its counter starts at zero and counts the meanings flagged for review, matching the checked rows.
The action tray uses the normal dark background colour instead of pure black; light mode retains its soft grey surface.

entries.summary: Clearer level and set controls, larger centred lookup icons, and a separate card action tray.
detail: Word range sits quietly at the top right; the selected level is wider with larger text and less surrounding padding. The lyrics-frequency sentence is hidden while its calculation remains available.
Set bars are taller with larger labels; the set summary and progress legend are centred and more subtle.
Commonness tooltips show a coloured icon and title above the explanation; Rare uses shares the sense meters’ bar proportions.
Larger lookup icons rise centred above the magnifying glass. Card-back actions sit on a separate black tray with a 10px gap; light mode uses soft grey.

entries.summary: Spanish and Portuguese 'de' (and pt 'em') cards now show 'of' / 'in; at' instead of stray senses like 'by means of' and 'in (wearing)' (candidate decks pt r4, es r6)
detail: LITERAL-GROUND. Only the preposition cards were re-run: pt de, do, da, dos, das, em, no, na, nos, nas (10 cards) and es de, del (2 cards). Every other card is byte-identical to pt r3 / es r5.

A rarer preposition sense must now beat the main one by 0.025, and de takes 'of' outright where it follows a verb or noun it belongs to (precisar de, gostaria de fazer, lembrar de mim, bolso da jaqueta).
Examples: pt dos went from 12 mixed rows to one 'of' row; pt da lost 'by means of' (5) and 'in (wearing)' (3); es de lost 'from' (13 of 80, mostly wrong) to 'of'.
Measured on 124 hand-judged changed sentences: 78 better, 7 worse where the card English changes (e.g. 'caiu da ponte' now 'of', should be 'from').
Not changed: por, para, es a / al / en (a prior made them worse), and the English-wording fix ('except' vs 'except for') is verified but not rolled out deck-wide yet.
No spend: WSD ran offline from the existing embedding cache.
